Write a table of personal data outside all repositories

Source: R/utils-private.R
write_private_csv.Rd

Some files exist for administration only, e-mail addresses for contacting participants being the typical case, and must never sit next to the data or inside a repository. write_private_csv() writes such a table to a private folder and refuses whenever that folder lies inside a git work tree, where one careless git add would publish it.

Usage

write_private_csv(
  x,
  file,
  dir = Sys.getenv("CATLAS_PRIVATE_DIR"),
  overwrite = FALSE
)

Arguments

x

A data frame.

file

Character(1). Path of the file within the private folder. It is a file name, optionally preceded by subfolders separated by /, e.g. "fba-allergy-online-02/naive.rds". Absolute paths and .. are refused.

dir

Character(1). The private folder. Defaults to the environment variable CATLAS_PRIVATE_DIR, which belongs in .Renviron.

overwrite

Logical(1). Replace an existing file? Defaults to FALSE.

Value

The path of the written file, invisibly.

Details

Repositories

A folder counts as inside a repository when it, or any folder above it, contains a .git entry. Checking for the entry rather than calling git works without git installed and also recognises worktrees and submodules, whose .git is a file.

Study folders

Keep the files of each study in a subfolder of the private folder named by its study identifier, e.g. "fba-allergy-online-02/naive.rds". Missing subfolders are created when writing. The folder to which the file is saved must lie inside the private folder and outside every repository.
